common_errors: Writing 'condensation' alone without the qualifier 'polymerization'
Confusing the process with 'photosynthesis' since it involves glucose
examiner_notes: Both 'Polymerization' and 'Condensation polymerization' are accepted; a bare answer of 'condensation' alone is not given credit.

common_errors: Writing 'chromatin' instead of 'centromere'
Writing 'kinetochore' as a substitute term
examiner_notes: Only 'Centromere' is accepted; 'kinetochore' is a related but distinct structure and is not credited.

common_errors: Writing 'hemocyanin' (the respiratory pigment in some invertebrates) instead of haemoglobin
Spelling it as 'hemoglobin' without the iron-containing qualifier confusion, or writing just 'iron' as the answer
examiner_notes: Either British ('haemoglobin') or American ('hemoglobin') spelling is accepted.

common_errors: Confusing ureter with urethra
Writing 'renal vein' or 'renal artery' instead of the excretory duct
examiner_notes: Spelling precision is expected since 'ureter' and 'urethra' are commonly confused; examiners specifically watch for this mix-up.

common_errors: Writing 'cerebellum' instead of 'cerebrum'
Writing 'hippocampus' (not part of the ICSE syllabus terminology at this level)
examiner_notes: Only 'Cerebrum' is accepted at this level; the cerebellum is associated with balance/coordination, not memory, in the ICSE syllabus.

common_errors: Confusing allele with gene itself, or with genotype
Omitting that alleles occupy the same locus on homologous chromosomes
Describing alleles only as 'different genes' without mentioning they control the same trait
examiner_notes: Full credit requires both the 'alternative form of a gene' idea and the 'same locus on homologous chromosomes' idea; a one-line vague definition may only get partial credit at the examiner's discretion.

common_errors: Omitting direction of movement (high to low concentration)
Confusing diffusion with osmosis by mentioning a semi-permeable membrane
Writing 'movement of molecules' without specifying liquid or gas
examiner_notes: The phrase 'higher to lower concentration' is essential; answers describing only 'spreading out' without this direction are marked incomplete.

common_errors: Omitting that it occurs in the light reaction / requires sunlight
Confusing photolysis with hydrolysis
Forgetting to mention that oxygen is released as a product
examiner_notes: Examiners expect 'splitting of water' plus the condition 'in presence of sunlight'; omitting sunlight/chlorophyll usually costs the mark.

common_errors: Confusing phenotype with genotype
Describing phenotype only as 'physical appearance' without linking it to genotype-environment interaction
examiner_notes: The definition must reference both genotype and environment interaction; stating only 'visible characteristics' without this link may receive partial credit.

common_errors: Omitting 'per unit area' and giving only 'number of individuals'
Confusing population density with birth rate or population growth rate
examiner_notes: Both 'number of individuals' and 'per unit area' must be present for the full mark.

common_errors: Writing 'androgen' as a generic term instead of the specific hormone 'testosterone'
Writing 'adrenaline' by confusing it with a stress-response hormone
examiner_notes: Only the specific hormone name 'Testosterone' is accepted for the mark.

common_errors: Writing 'pleura' (the lung covering) instead of 'pericardium'
Writing 'endocardium' or 'myocardium' by confusing heart wall layers with the outer covering
examiner_notes: Only 'Pericardium' is accepted; confusing it with the lung's pleura is a very common analogy-based error in this question format.

common_errors: Writing 'Islets of Langerhans' generically instead of specifying 'Alpha cells'
Writing 'Beta cells' by mistake since it was mentioned earlier in the analogy
examiner_notes: The specific cell type 'Alpha cells' is required; naming only the pancreas or Islets of Langerhans without specifying alpha cells does not earn full credit.

common_errors: Writing 'hepatic portal vein' instead of 'hepatic artery'
Writing 'renal artery' by mistakenly copying the analogy term instead of applying it to the liver
examiner_notes: Only 'Hepatic artery' is accepted; the hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine, not oxygenated blood, so it is not credited here.

common_errors: Writing 'implantation' by mistake, mirroring the analogy given for the uterus
Writing 'ovulation' instead of 'fertilization'
examiner_notes: Only 'Fertilization' is accepted since it is the process that occurs specifically in the fallopian tube.

common_errors: Placing Effector before Spinal cord
Placing Response before Effector
Starting the sequence correctly but reversing Receptor and Spinal cord
examiner_notes: No partial credit is given for a partially correct order; the entire sequence must match exactly for the mark.

common_errors: Reproducing the sequence exactly as it appears in the jumbled question rather than reordering it
Placing Xylem before Endodermis, reversing the correct order of water entry
examiner_notes: The biologically correct pathway of water movement is Root hair, Epidermis, Cortex, Endodermis, Xylem; evaluators should accept this correct physiological order as the primary answer even though some reference sources list an incorrect sequence.

common_errors: Placing Pupil before Aqueous humor, reversing the correct order light passes through the eye
Placing Yellow spot before Vitreous humor
examiner_notes: The full correct order (Conjunctiva, Aqueous humor, Pupil, Vitreous humor, Yellow spot) is required for the mark; no partial credit for a partially correct sequence.

common_errors: Placing Neanderthal Man after Cro-Magnon Man, reversing the correct evolutionary order
Omitting Homo erectus or placing it after Neanderthal Man
examiner_notes: The full correct evolutionary sequence is required for the mark; students often confuse the relative order of Neanderthal and Cro-Magnon man.

common_errors: Placing Capillaries directly after Artery, omitting Arteriole
Reversing the order of Venule and Vein
examiner_notes: The complete correct sequence (Artery, Arteriole, Capillaries, Venule, Vein) is required; no marks for a partially correct blood vessel order.

common_errors: Selecting (a) Reproduction instead of the specific process (c) Fertilization
Selecting (d) Embryo, confusing the product with the process
examiner_notes: Only the option letter and/or term need be written; both are accepted.

common_errors: Selecting (c) Eosinophils, Basophils, confusing granulocytes with agranulocytes
Selecting (b) Lymphocytes, Basophils, mixing one correct and one incorrect cell type
examiner_notes: Students must know that agranulocytes (Lymphocytes, Monocytes) lack visible cytoplasmic granules, unlike Eosinophils and Basophils.

common_errors: Selecting (a) Knee-jerk, mistakenly thinking it is a learned response
Selecting (d) Sneezing, not recognizing it as an unconditioned/natural reflex
examiner_notes: Salivation at the sight of food is a conditioned reflex, not a natural (unconditioned) reflex, which is why it is the correct choice for 'not a natural reflex action'.

common_errors: Selecting (b) Bowman's capsule, confusing a component of the nephron with the nephron itself
Selecting (c) Renal pelvis, confusing a collecting structure with the functional unit
examiner_notes: Only (d) Nephron is correct as the structural and functional unit; Bowman's capsule is a part of the nephron, not the whole unit.

common_errors: Selecting (a) 23 pairs of autosomes, forgetting that autosomes exclude sex chromosomes
Selecting (b), confusing the haploid ovum with the diploid somatic cell chromosome count
examiner_notes: Students must recall that the human ovum is haploid (23 chromosomes total: 22 autosomes + 1 X-chromosome), not diploid.

common_errors: Naming the odd term without stating the category, or vice versa
Selecting a plant hormone (e.g. Ethylene) as the odd one out instead of Adrenaline
examiner_notes: Both the correct odd term AND the correct category name are required together for the single mark; one without the other earns no credit.

common_errors: Selecting Tympanum as the odd term instead of Ear ossicles
Naming the category as 'parts of the ear' instead of specifically 'outer ear'
examiner_notes: The category must be specified precisely as 'outer ear', not just 'ear', since Ear ossicles also belong to the ear but to the middle ear.

common_errors: Selecting Soiled dressings as the odd term instead of Household detergents
Naming the category as 'hospital items' instead of the more precise 'biomedical/hospital waste'
examiner_notes: The category is best phrased as 'biomedical waste' or 'hospital waste'; a vague answer like 'medical things' may receive partial credit at the examiner's discretion.

common_errors: Selecting Cretinism or Myxoedema as the odd term instead of Simple Goitre
Describing the shared category only as 'thyroid disorders' without noting they arise from hormone imbalance rather than iodine deficiency
examiner_notes: The category should specify 'disorders due to abnormal thyroxine secretion', distinguishing them from Simple Goitre which is specifically due to iodine deficiency.

common_errors: Selecting one of the nitrogenous bases (e.g. Cytosine) as the odd term instead of Creatinine
Naming the category as 'DNA bases' without allowing for RNA, since Cytosine is common to both
examiner_notes: The category is best stated broadly as 'nitrogenous bases' to cover both DNA and RNA; overly narrow answers may still be credited if the odd term is correct.

common_errors: Writing 'Darwin's finches' or another evolution example instead of the peppered moth
Misspelling or mistranslating the scientific name without recognizing it as the peppered moth
examiner_notes: Recognizing 'Biston betularia' as the scientific name of the peppered moth (used as the classic example of industrial melanism) is essential.

common_errors: Writing 'sex organ' instead of the precise term 'Gonad'
Writing 'testosterone' (the hormone produced) instead of the category term 'Gonad'
examiner_notes: The precise biological term 'Gonad' is expected rather than a descriptive phrase.

common_errors: Writing 'Vitamin K' instead of 'Calcium', confusing two different clotting factors
Writing 'Fibrinogen' instead of the specific ion 'Calcium'
examiner_notes: Only 'Calcium' (Factor IV) is accepted as the match; other clotting factors like Vitamin K or Fibrinogen are not credited here.

common_errors: Writing 'light reaction' instead of 'light independent reaction', reversing the two stages of photosynthesis
Writing 'grana' instead of 'stroma', confusing the two chloroplast compartments
examiner_notes: Students must correctly associate stroma with the light-independent (dark) reaction, as opposed to grana which is the site of the light reaction.

common_errors: Writing 'transpiration' instead of the more general 'diffusion of gases'
Writing 'photosynthesis' since stomata are involved in gas exchange for that process specifically
examiner_notes: The expected general answer is 'diffusion of gases' (covering both O2/CO2 exchange and water vapour loss); 'transpiration' alone may be considered too narrow by some examiners.

common_errors: Writing 'phototropism' by confusing it with light-based tropism rather than chemical
Writing 'hydrotropism' by confusing the pollen tube's water-related movement with chemical attraction
examiner_notes: Correct identification depends on interpreting the given diagram of pollen tube growth toward the ovule; only 'Chemotropism' is accepted.

common_errors: Giving a generic tropism definition without specifying 'chemical stimulus'
Failing to link the explanation back to a plant part such as the pollen tube
examiner_notes: The explanation must specifically mention 'chemical stimulus' to distinguish chemotropism from other tropisms.

common_errors: Writing 'pollen grain' instead of 'pollen tube'
Writing 'style' by confusing the structure with the pathway it grows through
examiner_notes: Correct labelling depends entirely on the given diagram; only 'Pollen tube' is accepted for part A.

common_errors: Writing that it is attracted to 'sunlight' instead of chemical substances from the ovule
Omitting mention that the attractants guide the tube specifically toward the ovary/ovule
examiner_notes: The answer must specify that the pollen tube is attracted to chemical substances (attractants) released by the ovule, not a generic stimulus.

common_errors: Giving Mimosa pudica as the example when the intended answer per this scheme is a tendril-bearing climber
Naming a plant that shows a different tropism (e.g. sunflower for phototropism) by mistake
examiner_notes: Both a tendril-bearing climber (e.g. pea, cucumber, grapevine) and Mimosa pudica are commonly cited in textbooks; examiners generally accept either as thigmotropism examples, though the reference answer favours the touch-me-not plant.

common_errors: Writing 'oxygen' instead of 'carbon dioxide', misreading the role of KOH in the setup
Writing 'sunlight' or 'chlorophyll' instead of recognizing the specific variable being tested
examiner_notes: Correct identification depends on recognizing that KOH (which absorbs CO2) is the key experimental variable shown in the diagram.

common_errors: Writing that KOH 'produces oxygen' instead of absorbing carbon dioxide
Omitting that the purpose is to deprive the enclosed leaf of CO2 for testing
examiner_notes: The answer must state that KOH absorbs carbon dioxide from the flask, not merely that it is present; linking this to depriving the leaf of CO2 strengthens the answer.

common_errors: Omitting either carbon dioxide or water as a raw material
Omitting the by-product oxygen or forgetting to mention chlorophyll/sunlight as conditions
examiner_notes: A complete definition requires raw materials (CO2 and water), conditions (sunlight and chlorophyll), and product (carbohydrate/food); partial definitions may receive partial credit.

common_errors: Stating the leaf 'turns blue-black' by mistakenly describing the control leaf instead of leaf A
Omitting the reason (absence of CO2) for the negative starch test
examiner_notes: The answer should state both the observation (no blue-black colour / remains colourless) and the reason (CO2 unavailable) for full credit.

common_errors: Unbalanced equation; omitting the conditions (sunlight/chlorophyll) above the arrow
Forgetting to show water as both a reactant and, in the fuller equation, a product
examiner_notes: Both the simplified (6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2) and fuller (6CO2 + 12H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2 + 6H2O) balanced forms are accepted, provided sunlight and chlorophyll are indicated as conditions.

common_errors: Confusing which numbered vessel carries oxygenated versus deoxygenated blood
Writing 'vein' or 'artery' generically instead of the specific named vessel
examiner_notes: All four labels must be correct, based on the given circulation flow diagram, for the mark to be awarded.

common_errors: Writing 'pulmonary artery' or 'pulmonary vein' instead of 'coronary artery'
Confusing blood supply to the lungs with blood supply to the heart's own muscle tissue
examiner_notes: The correct answer to this question about the heart's own muscle supply is coronary artery; a reference answer describing pulmonary veins is not biologically correct here, since pulmonary veins relate to lung-to-heart circulation, not the heart's own blood supply.

common_errors: Naming vessel 5 correctly but omitting that it carries nutrient-rich blood specifically from the small intestine
Confusing the hepatic portal vein with the hepatic artery or hepatic vein
examiner_notes: The answer should identify the vessel as the hepatic portal vein and explain its role in carrying nutrient-rich blood to the liver, not merely name it.

common_errors: Writing 'systemic circulation' instead of 'pulmonary circulation'
Writing 'double circulation' as a generic answer instead of the specific type between heart and lungs
examiner_notes: Only 'Pulmonary circulation' is accepted for the specific heart-lung pathway.

common_errors: Omitting platelets; mislabelling granulocyte nuclei shapes
Drawing only erythrocytes and one or two leucocyte types instead of all five types
examiner_notes: All major blood cell types must be shown and correctly labelled for the mark; diagrams missing platelets or with incorrect nuclear shapes for granulocytes typically lose credit.

common_errors: Naming the correct defect (Myopia) but the wrong lens (convex instead of concave)
Confusing Myopia with Hypermetropia based on the direction of the ray diagram
examiner_notes: Both the defect name and the corrective lens type must be correctly identified together, based on the given ray diagram, for the mark.

common_errors: Confusing the cause of Myopia with that of Hypermetropia (e.g. writing 'shortening of eyeball')
Omitting mention of where the image forms as a result of the cause
examiner_notes: Either elongation of the eyeball or excessive curvature of the lens/cornea is accepted as a valid cause.

common_errors: Writing 'behind the retina' instead of 'in front of the retina'
Writing 'on the retina', missing the point that the defect causes incorrect image formation
examiner_notes: Only 'In front of the retina' is accepted, consistent with the myopic defect described in part (i).

common_errors: Naming the layers out of order or omitting the innermost layer (Retina)
Confusing Choroid with Cornea
examiner_notes: All three layers (Sclera, Choroid, Retina) must be named, ideally in order from outermost to innermost, for full credit.

common_errors: Omitting the node of Ranvier or myelin sheath labels
Drawing the axon without showing branched dendrites at the cell body
examiner_notes: All key parts (dendrites, cyton with nucleus, axon, myelin sheath, node of Ranvier, axon terminal) must be present and labelled; unlabelled diagrams typically do not receive full credit.

common_errors: Stating only that plants 'look nice' or 'purify water' without linking to oxygen release via photosynthesis
Omitting that the oxygen is used by fish/aquatic organisms for respiration
examiner_notes: The biological reason must explicitly connect photosynthesis, oxygen release, and its use by aquatic organisms for respiration.

common_errors: Giving only a general statement like 'it is harmful' without explaining the effect on organisms/ecosystems
Omitting that both humans and aquatic organisms are affected by contaminated water
examiner_notes: A complete answer should mention the introduction of harmful substances and their effect on both aquatic life and human health/ecosystem balance.

common_errors: Confusing rod cells and cone cells, attributing colour vision to rods
Omitting that rods function in dim light but cannot distinguish colour
examiner_notes: The reason must correctly attribute colour vision to cone cells (inactive in dim light) and distinguish their role from rod cells.

common_errors: Stating only that 'medicine improved health' without linking it to reduced death rate
Omitting the causal chain: fewer deaths from disease leads to population rise
examiner_notes: The answer should clearly state the causal link between reduced death rate (due to control of infectious disease) and the rise in population.

common_errors: Describing only physical features (e.g. upright posture) without mentioning brain size/intelligence
Omitting comparison with earlier hominid species
examiner_notes: A strong answer links large brain size (relative to body) with intelligence, tool use, and language to justify the 'most highly evolved' status.

common_errors: Writing 'medulla' instead of 'cortex', confusing the two regions of the kidney
Writing 'nephron' as the region instead of the region within the kidney
examiner_notes: Correct identification depends on recognizing the structure (e.g. glomerulus/Bowman's capsule) as being located in the cortex, based on the given diagram.

common_errors: Confusing afferent and efferent arterioles (reversing which carries blood in vs. out)
Writing 'renal artery' instead of 'afferent arteriole' for the specific labelled part
examiner_notes: All four labels must be correct, based on the given nephron diagram, for the mark to be awarded.

common_errors: Writing 'filtration' instead of the more precise technical term 'ultrafiltration'
Writing 'reabsorption', confusing it with the subsequent tubular process
examiner_notes: The precise ICSE-specified technical term 'Ultrafiltration' is expected rather than the general term 'filtration'.

common_errors: Stating only 'it is not concentrated enough' without naming the useful substances still present
Omitting that glucose and amino acids are examples of substances not yet reabsorbed
examiner_notes: A full answer should name specific useful substances (e.g. glucose, amino acids) still present in fluid X to justify why it isn't yet urine.

common_errors: Omitting renal blood vessels or the urethra
Drawing only one kidney or missing one ureter
examiner_notes: All parts (kidneys, renal artery/vein, ureters, urinary bladder, urethra) must be shown and labelled for full credit.

common_errors: Giving only one side of the comparison
Confusing hydathodes with stomata as the site of guttation
examiner_notes: Both sites of occurrence (stomata/lenticels for transpiration and hydathodes for guttation) must be stated for the mark.

common_errors: Giving an example that does not clearly belong to one category (e.g. mixed waste)
Reversing the examples, e.g. calling plastic biodegradable
examiner_notes: A valid example of each type is required together for the mark; any commonly accepted example is credited.

common_errors: Describing objectives too vaguely (e.g. 'to improve India') without specifying the actual goal
Confusing the objective of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan with general environmental conservation
examiner_notes: A correct objective must be stated for both programmes together for the mark; vague or generic statements may not be credited.

common_errors: Describing osmosis as movement of 'solutes' instead of specifically 'water molecules'
Omitting that active transport requires energy (ATP), a key distinguishing feature
examiner_notes: The substances involved (water for osmosis vs. solutes/ions for active transport) must be correctly stated for both processes for the mark.

common_errors: Reversing the positions, e.g. describing chromosomes moving to poles as metaphase
Omitting the term 'equatorial plane' for metaphase
examiner_notes: Both chromosome positions (equatorial plane in metaphase; moving to poles in anaphase) must be correctly stated for the mark.

common_errors: Stating the mercury level falls instead of rises
Naming the conducting tissue as phloem instead of xylem
examiner_notes: Both the direction of mercury movement (rises) and the correct tissue (xylem) must be stated together for the mark.

common_errors: Omitting 'excess' water, implying all water loss rather than surplus water
Omitting that it occurs mainly through stomata
examiner_notes: The definition should specify loss of water vapour from aerial parts, mainly via stomata, for full credit.

common_errors: Stating that low humidity decreases the rate of transpiration (reversed logic)
Giving only one of the two conditions asked for
examiner_notes: Both conditions (less humidity and high temperature) must be addressed, and both correctly stated as increasing the rate of transpiration, for the mark.

common_errors: Giving only one advantage instead of two
Describing a disadvantage (e.g. water loss) instead of an advantage
examiner_notes: Any two valid advantages (e.g. suction pull for water transport, cooling effect, gaseous exchange) are accepted; only one correct advantage earns partial credit at most.

common_errors: Failing to show cell wall retaining shape while protoplast shrinks
Omitting the plasmolysing solution surrounding the cell in the diagram
examiner_notes: The diagram must clearly distinguish the rigid, unchanged cell wall from the shrunken protoplast pulled away from it, with correct labelling, for full credit.

common_errors: Writing 'tympanum' or 'ear ossicles' instead of the sensory organ specifically within the cochlea
Writing 'cochlea' itself instead of the structure inside it
examiner_notes: Only 'Organ of Corti' is accepted as the precise sensory structure within the cochlea.

common_errors: Writing 'death rate' instead of 'birth rate'
Writing 'population growth rate', confusing it with the specific term for live births
examiner_notes: Only 'Birth rate' is accepted for this specific technical term.

common_errors: Writing 'neuron junction' instead of the precise term 'synapse'
Writing 'node of Ranvier', confusing it with the point of contact between neurons
examiner_notes: Only 'Synapse' is accepted as the precise technical term.

common_errors: Writing 'prostate gland' instead of 'bulbourethral gland (Cowper's gland)'
Writing 'seminal vesicle', confusing accessory gland functions
examiner_notes: Both 'Bulbourethral gland' and 'Cowper's gland' are accepted as correct terms.

common_errors: Writing 'hyperglycemia' instead of 'hypoglycemia', reversing the prefix meaning
Writing 'diabetes' instead of the specific low-sugar condition
examiner_notes: Only 'Hypoglycemia' is accepted for a lowered blood sugar condition; students often confuse the hyper-/hypo- prefixes.

common_errors: Writing 'ciliary muscle' instead of 'iris', confusing structures involved in different eye functions
Writing 'pupil' itself instead of the structure that adjusts its size
examiner_notes: Only 'Iris' is accepted as the structure that adjusts pupil size.

common_errors: Writing 'tubectomy' instead of 'vasectomy', confusing the male and female surgical methods
Writing 'castration' incorrectly as a synonym for vasectomy
examiner_notes: Only 'Vasectomy' is accepted for the male surgical sterilization method; tubectomy is the female equivalent and is not credited.

common_errors: Writing 'phagocytosis' instead of 'diapedesis', confusing WBC functions
Writing 'osmosis' or 'diffusion' generically instead of the specific term
examiner_notes: Only 'Diapedesis' is accepted as the precise term for leucocyte migration through capillary walls.

common_errors: Writing 'variation' instead of 'mutation', confusing general genetic diversity with sudden change
Writing 'crossing over' instead of the specific term for gene change
examiner_notes: Only 'Mutation' is accepted for a sudden inheritable change in genes.

common_errors: Writing 'G1 phase' or 'G2 phase' instead of 'S-phase', confusing the sub-phases of interphase
Writing 'interphase' generically instead of the specific sub-phase
examiner_notes: Only 'S-phase (Synthesis phase)' is accepted as the specific sub-phase of interphase where DNA replication occurs.

common_errors: Naming only one function (hearing) and omitting balance/equilibrium
Confusing balance function with the cerebellum's role instead of the ear's
examiner_notes: Both functions (hearing and balance) must be stated for the mark; one alone earns only partial credit at most.

common_errors: Naming only fruit ripening and omitting the senescence/abscission function
Confusing ethylene's role with that of auxin (e.g. citing cell elongation)
examiner_notes: Both functions (fruit ripening and senescence/abscission) must be stated for the mark.

common_errors: Naming only the moistening/washing function and omitting the antibacterial (lysozyme) function
Omitting the specific mention of the enzyme lysozyme
examiner_notes: Both functions (mechanical washing/moistening and antibacterial action via lysozyme) must be stated for the mark.

common_errors: Naming only sperm production and omitting the hormone secretion function
Writing 'produces ova' by confusing testis with ovary
examiner_notes: Both functions (sperm production and testosterone secretion) must be stated for the mark.

common_errors: Naming only balance/posture and omitting coordination of voluntary movements
Confusing cerebellum's function with that of the cerebrum (e.g. citing memory or intelligence)
examiner_notes: Both functions (posture/balance and coordination of voluntary movement) must be stated for the mark.

common_errors: Writing 'glucagon' instead of 'insulin', reversing the two pancreatic hormones
Writing 'glycogen' (the storage product) instead of the hormone name
examiner_notes: Only 'Insulin' is accepted as the hormone that converts excess glucose to glycogen.

common_errors: Writing 'liver' instead of 'pancreas', confusing the site of glycogen storage with the site of hormone secretion
Writing 'Islets of Langerhans' without the broader gland name 'pancreas'
examiner_notes: 'Pancreas' is expected; 'Islets of Langerhans' may be accepted as a more specific correct answer at the examiner's discretion.

common_errors: Writing 'hypothalamus' instead of 'pituitary gland', confusing the two brain-associated endocrine structures
Omitting the qualifier 'anterior' when naming the pituitary
examiner_notes: 'Pituitary gland' is accepted generally; specifying 'anterior pituitary' shows more precise knowledge but is not strictly required.

common_errors: Describing a function of a different hormone (e.g. thyroxine) instead of growth hormone
Giving an overly vague answer like 'helps growth' without mentioning cells, muscles, or bones
examiner_notes: The function should specifically mention stimulation of growth in body cells, muscles, and bones for full credit.

common_errors: Writing 'thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH)' instead of 'thyroxine', confusing the pituitary hormone that regulates the thyroid with the thyroid's own hormone
Misspelling 'thyroxine' as 'thyroxin' (both are generally accepted)
examiner_notes: Only 'Thyroxine' is accepted as the hormone secreted by the thyroid gland itself, not TSH which is secreted by the pituitary.

common_errors: Giving only 'controls metabolism' without mentioning brain development or bone maintenance
Confusing thyroxine's function with that of growth hormone
examiner_notes: A complete answer should mention regulation of metabolic rate along with its role in brain development and bone maintenance.

common_errors: Writing 'cortisol' instead of 'adrenaline', confusing the two adrenal hormones
Writing 'noradrenaline' instead of the more commonly expected 'adrenaline'
examiner_notes: 'Adrenaline' is the expected answer; 'noradrenaline' may be accepted as a related hormone at the examiner's discretion.

common_errors: Writing 'pituitary gland' instead of 'adrenal gland', confusing which gland secretes emergency hormones
Omitting the qualifier 'medulla' when naming the adrenal gland
examiner_notes: 'Adrenal gland' is accepted generally; specifying 'adrenal medulla' shows more precise knowledge but is not strictly required.

common_errors: Writing 'hypothalamus' instead of 'posterior pituitary', since oxytocin is released from the posterior pituitary though produced in the hypothalamus
Writing 'anterior pituitary' instead of the correct posterior lobe
examiner_notes: 'Posterior pituitary' is the ICSE-expected answer for the gland that secretes/releases oxytocin.

common_errors: Confusing oxytocin's function with that of prolactin (milk production) instead of uterine contractions
Giving a vague answer like 'helps in childbirth' without mentioning uterine contractions specifically
examiner_notes: The function should specifically mention stimulation of uterine contractions during childbirth (labour) for full credit.

common_errors: Giving only the phenotype or only the genotype, omitting the other
Writing the genotype incorrectly as TTRr or TtRR instead of TtRr
examiner_notes: Both phenotype (tall, red flowers) and genotype (TtRr) must be stated together for the mark.

common_errors: Missing one or more of the four gamete combinations
Writing incorrect combinations such as TT or Rr instead of single-allele gametes
examiner_notes: All four gamete combinations (TR, Tr, tR, tr) must be listed for the mark; missing even one combination results in no credit.

common_errors: Writing '3:1' by mistakenly applying the monohybrid ratio instead of the dihybrid ratio
Writing the ratio in the wrong order (e.g. 1:3:3:9)
examiner_notes: Only the correct dihybrid ratio '9:3:3:1' in the correct order is accepted.

common_errors: Confusing the Law of Independent Assortment with the Law of Segregation
Omitting that the law applies specifically when two pairs of traits are considered together
examiner_notes: The statement must specify that it applies to two (or more) gene pairs assorting independently, distinguishing it from the Law of Segregation which concerns a single gene pair.

common_errors: Naming an autosomal disorder (e.g. sickle cell anemia) instead of an X-linked one
Naming only one disorder instead of two
examiner_notes: Colour blindness and Haemophilia are the standard ICSE examples; Duchenne muscular dystrophy is also accepted as a valid alternative.

common_errors: Confusing the umbilical cord with the placenta in labelling
Mislabelling amniotic fluid as the amniotic sac/membrane itself
examiner_notes: All three labels must be correct, based on the given foetus diagram, for the mark to be awarded.

common_errors: Naming only nutrient/oxygen supply and omitting waste removal
Confusing the placenta's function with that of the umbilical cord
examiner_notes: Two correct functions of the placenta (e.g. nutrient/oxygen supply and waste removal) are required together for the mark; secreting pregnancy hormones is also accepted as a valid alternative function.

common_errors: Describing amniotic fluid's role only as 'protection' without mentioning free movement of the foetus
Confusing amniotic fluid with the placenta's nutritive role
examiner_notes: A complete answer should mention both protection from mechanical shock and allowing free movement of the foetus.

common_errors: Defining gestation vaguely as 'pregnancy' without specifying it as the foetal development period from conception to birth
Giving an incorrect duration (e.g. 9 months only, without the more precise 280 days/40 weeks)
examiner_notes: Both the definition and the correct duration (about 280 days / 40 weeks / 9 months) must be given together for the mark.

common_errors: Reversing XX and XY between male and female
Omitting the terms 'homogametic'/'heterogametic' though these are not strictly required
examiner_notes: Both combinations (XY for male, XX for female) must be stated correctly and clearly attributed to the correct sex for the mark.
